category: Text Analytics Toolbox > Text Preparation, Bag-of-Words, Topic Models, Embeddings & Transformers
description: Functions of Text Analytics Toolbox for importing and tokenizing text, cleaning and normalizing documents, counting words and n-grams, topic modeling, sentiment and keyword extraction, word embeddings, BERT transformers and document similarity.

tools.name: tokenizedDocument
tools.description: Creates an array of tokenized documents from text, splitting it into words, punctuation and detected patterns such as URLs, emails, hashtags and emoticons. It is the central data type for almost every Text Analytics Toolbox preprocessing and modeling function.
tools.usage:
documents = tokenizedDocument(str)
documents = tokenizedDocument(str, Name=Value)

parameters.name: str
parameters.description: String array, character vector or cell array of text; each element becomes one document.

parameters.name: DetectPatterns
parameters.description: Patterns to keep as single tokens: "all" or any of "email-address", "web-address", "hashtag", "at-mention", "emoticon", "emoji", "digits".

parameters.name: CustomTokens / RegularExpressions
parameters.description: Extra tokens or regex patterns that must not be split.

parameters.name: TokenizeMethod
parameters.description: "unicode", "mecab" (Japanese/Korean) or "none" when str is already tokenized.

tools.notes: Most string functions (lower, contains, replace, regexprep) have tokenizedDocument overloads. Use string(documents) or joinWords to convert back to text.

tools.name: extractFileText
tools.description: Reads the text content of plain-text, PDF, Microsoft Word (.docx) and HTML files or web pages into a string. It is the usual entry point for building a corpus from a folder of documents.
tools.usage:
str = extractFileText(filename)
str = extractFileText(filename, Name=Value)

parameters.name: filename
parameters.description: Path or URL of a .txt, .pdf, .docx, .htm/.html file.

parameters.name: Pages
parameters.description: Page numbers to read from a PDF.

tools.notes: Scanned PDFs contain no text layer; use ocr (Computer Vision Toolbox) instead. Use readPDFFormData for PDF form fields and fileDatastore with ReadFcn=@extractFileText for large collections.

tools.name: extractHTMLText
tools.description: Extracts readable text from HTML code or a parsed htmlTree, dropping markup, scripts and styles. The article mode tries to keep only the main content of a web page.
tools.usage:
str = extractHTMLText(code)
str = extractHTMLText(tree)
str = extractHTMLText(___, ExtractionMethod=method)

parameters.name: code / tree
parameters.description: HTML as a string, or an htmlTree object.

parameters.name: ExtractionMethod
parameters.description: "tree" (default, paragraphs of the whole tree), "article" (main article body) or "all-text" (all text, including non-visible).

tools.notes: Use htmlTree + findElement to extract specific elements (tables, links) before extracting text. eraseTags removes tags from text that is not full HTML.

tools.name: htmlTree
tools.description: Parses HTML code into a tree object that can be queried with CSS selectors via findElement, and whose attributes and text can be read with getAttribute and extractHTMLText. Useful for web scraping specific elements of a page.
tools.usage:
tree = htmlTree(code)
subtrees = findElement(tree, selector)
attr = getAttribute(tree, name)

parameters.name: code
parameters.description: HTML code as string or character vector.

parameters.name: selector
parameters.description: CSS selector for findElement, e.g. "a", "div.content p", "table#results td".

tools.notes: Missing attributes are returned as missing strings; filter them with ismissing. The root of a subtree can be converted back to HTML with string(tree).

tools.name: erasePunctuation
tools.description: Removes punctuation characters and symbols from text or tokenized documents. It is a standard cleaning step before building bag-of-words models.
tools.usage:
newStr = erasePunctuation(str)
newDocuments = erasePunctuation(documents)
newDocuments = erasePunctuation(documents, TokenTypes=types)

parameters.name: TokenTypes
parameters.description: Token types to process, e.g. "all" or {'letters','other'}; by default detected patterns such as emails and URLs are left intact.

tools.example:
documents = tokenizedDocument("Hello, world!!! Visit https://example.com :)");
documents = erasePunctuation(documents)
tools.notes: Run it after tokenizing so that detected web addresses, emoticons and hashtags survive. Removing punctuation before splitSentences destroys sentence boundaries.

tools.name: eraseURLs
tools.description: Removes HTTP and HTTPS web addresses from text or documents. Use it when cleaning social media, email or web-scraped text where links carry no useful words.
tools.usage:
newStr = eraseURLs(str)
newDocuments = eraseURLs(documents)
tools.example:
str = "Read the docs at https://www.mathworks.com/help and http://example.org now";
newStr = eraseURLs(str)
tools.notes: Related cleaning functions: eraseTags (HTML/XML tags), decodeHTMLEntities (& etc.), erasePunctuation.

tools.name: removeStopWords
tools.description: Removes common function words such as "a", "the" and "in" from tokenized documents using a built-in language-specific stop list. Removing stop words reduces vocabulary size and emphasizes content words for counting-based models.
tools.usage:
newDocuments = removeStopWords(documents)
newDocuments = removeStopWords(documents, IgnoreCase=tf)

parameters.name: IgnoreCase
parameters.description: true (default) to match stop words regardless of case.

tools.example:
documents = tokenizedDocument("This is an example of a document about the weather.");
documents = removeStopWords(documents)
tools.notes: Do not remove stop words before addPartOfSpeechDetails, sentiment analysis (negations like "not") or transformer models. Use removeWords(documents, stopWords) for a custom list.

tools.name: stopWords
tools.description: Returns the built-in list of stop words for a language as a string array. Use it to inspect, extend or prune the list before calling removeWords.
tools.usage:
words = stopWords
words = stopWords(Language=language)
tools.notes: removeWords also accepts a bagOfWords model to remove words from the vocabulary.

tools.name: removeShortWords
tools.description: Removes words with a given number of characters or fewer from documents or a bag-of-words model. Often used to drop stray letters and abbreviations left after punctuation removal.
tools.usage:
newDocuments = removeShortWords(documents, len)
newBag = removeShortWords(bag, len)

parameters.name: len
parameters.description: Maximum length of words to remove (words with length <= len are removed).

tools.example:
documents = tokenizedDocument("An example of a short sentence with x y z tokens");
documents = removeShortWords(documents, 2)
tools.notes: removeLongWords removes words with length >= len, useful for stripping hashes, IDs or corrupted tokens.

tools.name: normalizeWords
tools.description: Reduces words to a root form by Porter stemming (default) or dictionary lemmatization, so that variants like "walking", "walked" and "walks" count as one term. Works on tokenized documents or string arrays of words.
tools.usage:
newDocuments = normalizeWords(documents)
newWords = normalizeWords(words)
newDocuments = normalizeWords(___, Style=style)

parameters.name: Language
parameters.description: Language of the words (stemming supports English; other languages vary).

tools.notes: Stems are not always real words ("studi"). For lemmatization, call addPartOfSpeechDetails first for better accuracy.

tools.name: replaceWords
tools.description: Replaces whole words in tokenized documents, for example to merge synonyms, expand abbreviations or map spelling variants to a canonical form.
tools.usage:
newDocuments = replaceWords(documents, oldWords, newWord)
newDocuments = replaceWords(documents, oldWords, newWords)
newDocuments = replaceWords(___, IgnoreCase=tf)

parameters.name: oldWords
parameters.description: Word or string array of words to replace.

parameters.name: newWord / newWords
parameters.description: Replacement word(s), scalar or same size as oldWords.

tools.example:
documents = tokenizedDocument("The colour of the car is grey");
documents = replaceWords(documents, ["colour" "grey"], ["color" "gray"])
tools.notes: replaceNgrams replaces multi-word sequences; replace works on substrings rather than whole tokens.

tools.name: splitSentences
tools.description: Splits text or tokenized documents into sentences, handling abbreviations and punctuation rules. Use it to create sentence-level documents for summarization, sentiment or embedding analyses.
tools.usage:
newStr = splitSentences(str)
newDocuments = splitSentences(documents)
tools.notes: Use addSentenceDetails to label sentence numbers without splitting, and splitParagraphs for paragraph-level splitting. Customize with the abbreviations table.

tools.name: addPartOfSpeechDetails
tools.description: Tags each token with its part of speech (noun, verb, adjective, proper noun, ...). The tags are shown by tokenDetails and are used by lemmatization, keyword extraction and custom filtering.
tools.usage:
updatedDocuments = addPartOfSpeechDetails(documents)
updatedDocuments = addPartOfSpeechDetails(documents, Name=Value)

parameters.name: Abbreviations
parameters.description: Table of abbreviations for sentence detection.

parameters.name: DiscardKnownValues
parameters.description: Recompute tags even if already present.

tools.notes: Run on raw documents (before stop-word and punctuation removal) for best accuracy. Supports English, Japanese, German and Korean.

tools.name: addEntityDetails
tools.description: Performs named entity recognition, labeling tokens as person, location, organization, other or non-entity. Read the labels with tokenDetails to extract names, places and companies from text.
tools.usage:
updatedDocuments = addEntityDetails(documents)
updatedDocuments = addEntityDetails(documents, Name=Value)

parameters.name: DiscardKnownValues
parameters.description: Recompute entities that are already set.

tools.notes: For custom entity types train an hmmEntityModel with trainHMMEntityModel. Supports English, Japanese, German and Korean.

tools.name: tokenDetails
tools.description: Returns a table with one row per token of a tokenized document array: the token text, document and line numbers, token type (letters, digits, punctuation, email-address, ...) and language, plus any sentence, part-of-speech, lemma, entity or dependency details that were added.
tools.usage: tdetails = tokenDetails(documents)
tools.notes: Add columns with addSentenceDetails, addPartOfSpeechDetails, addLemmaDetails, addEntityDetails, addDependencyDetails or addTypeDetails.

tools.name: context
tools.description: Searches documents for occurrences of a word or n-gram and returns them with surrounding text (keyword-in-context concordance), along with the document and word indices.
tools.usage:
tbl = context(documents, word)
tbl = context(documents, ngram)
tbl = context(___, numChars)

parameters.name: word / ngram
parameters.description: Word, or string array of consecutive words.

parameters.name: numChars
parameters.description: Number of characters of context on each side (default 20).

tools.notes: Case-sensitive; lowercase documents first to catch all variants.

tools.name: correctSpelling
tools.description: Corrects misspelled words in tokenized documents using a Hunspell-style dictionary and edit distance. Domain vocabulary can be protected with a list of known words.
tools.usage:
updatedDocuments = correctSpelling(documents)
updatedDocuments = correctSpelling(documents, Name=Value)

parameters.name: KnownWords
parameters.description: Additional words (jargon, product names) to treat as correctly spelled.

parameters.name: MaxEditDistance
parameters.description: Maximum edit distance for candidate corrections.

tools.example:
documents = tokenizedDocument("This documnet has sevral spelling erors in MATLAB.");
documents = correctSpelling(documents, KnownWords="MATLAB")
tools.notes: English only. Consider adding domain terms to KnownWords to avoid unwanted replacements. editDistanceSearcher offers custom nearest-word search.

tools.name: editDistance
tools.description: Computes the Levenshtein (or Damerau-Levenshtein, with swaps) edit distance between two strings or two tokenized documents, with configurable insertion, deletion, substitution and swap costs.
tools.usage:
d = editDistance(str1, str2)
d = editDistance(document1, document2)
d = editDistance(___, Name=Value)

parameters.name: SwapCost
parameters.description: Cost of transposing adjacent elements (default Inf, i.e. plain Levenshtein).

tools.example:
d = editDistance("MATLAB", "MATLAP")          % 1
d2 = editDistance("form", "from", SwapCost=1)   % 1 with transpositions
tools.notes: For documents the distance is computed over tokens, not characters. Use editDistanceSearcher with knnsearch/rangesearch to find nearest vocabulary words.

tools.name: bagOfWords
tools.description: Creates a bag-of-words model that records the word counts of each document in a sparse Counts matrix together with the Vocabulary. It is the input for topic models, tf-idf weighting, word clouds and classic machine learning classifiers.
tools.usage:
bag = bagOfWords(documents)
bag = bagOfWords(uniqueWords, counts)

parameters.name: uniqueWords, counts
parameters.description: Vocabulary and a documents-by-words count matrix to build a bag directly.

tools.example:
documents = tokenizedDocument(["an example of a short sentence" "a second short sentence"]);
bag = bagOfWords(documents)
full(bag.Counts)
bag.Vocabulary
tools.notes: Properties: Counts (sparse NumDocuments-by-NumWords), Vocabulary, NumWords, NumDocuments. Use addDocument/removeDocument to update and bagOfNgrams for multi-word features.

tools.name: bagOfNgrams
tools.description: Creates a bag-of-n-grams model that counts sequences of consecutive words (bigrams, trigrams, ...) per document. N-grams capture phrases such as "heat exchanger" that single words miss.
tools.usage:
bag = bagOfNgrams(documents)
bag = bagOfNgrams(documents, NgramLengths=lengths)

parameters.name: NgramLengths
parameters.description: N-gram lengths to count, e.g. 2 (default) or [1 2 3].

tools.notes: Properties Ngrams (string matrix) and Counts. Use removeInfrequentNgrams to prune rare n-grams.

tools.name: removeInfrequentWords
tools.description: Removes words that appear at most a given total number of times from a bag-of-words model. Pruning rare words shrinks the feature space and reduces noise from typos.
tools.usage: newBag = removeInfrequentWords(bag, count)

parameters.name: count
parameters.description: Words with total count <= count are removed.

tools.notes: After pruning some documents may become empty; remove them with removeEmptyDocuments and keep idx to align labels.

tools.name: removeEmptyDocuments
tools.description: Removes documents with no tokens from a tokenized document array, bag-of-words or bag-of-n-grams model, and returns the indices of the removed documents so labels can be kept in sync.
tools.usage:
newDocuments = removeEmptyDocuments(documents)
[newBag, idx] = removeEmptyDocuments(bag)
tools.example:
[documents, idx] = removeEmptyDocuments(documents);
labels(idx) = [];
tools.notes: Empty documents cause errors or NaNs in fitlda, tfidf and embeddings.

tools.name: topkwords
tools.description: Returns a table of the k most frequent words of a bag-of-words model, or the k highest-probability words of a topic in an LDA model. Used to summarize corpora and label topics.
tools.usage:
tbl = topkwords(bag)
tbl = topkwords(bag, k)
tbl = topkwords(ldaMdl, k, topicIdx)
tbl = topkwords(___, Name=Value)
tools.notes: Returns a table with Word and Count (bag) or Score (LDA). topkngrams is the n-gram counterpart.

tools.name: tfidf
tools.description: Computes the term frequency-inverse document frequency matrix from a bag-of-words model, weighting words that are frequent in a document but rare in the corpus. The result is a sparse feature matrix for classifiers, clustering or similarity search.
tools.usage:
M = tfidf(bag)
M = tfidf(bag, documents)
M = tfidf(___, Name=Value)

parameters.name: documents
parameters.description: New documents to weight using the bag's IDF (e.g. test set).

parameters.name: Normalized
parameters.description: Normalize rows to unit length (default false).

tools.notes: Always compute test features with the training bag so columns align. Output is sparse; many Statistics and Machine Learning Toolbox linear learners accept sparse input.

tools.name: encode
tools.description: Encodes documents (or individual words) as a sparse matrix of word or n-gram counts using the vocabulary of an existing bag-of-words or bag-of-n-grams model. Use it to featurize new documents consistently with a trained model.
tools.usage:
counts = encode(bag, documents)
counts = encode(bag, words)
counts = encode(___, DocumentsIn=dir)

parameters.name: DocumentsIn
parameters.description: "rows" (default) or "columns"; orientation of the output matrix.

tools.example:
bag = bagOfWords(trainDocs);
XNew = encode(bag, tokenizedDocument("pump leaking oil"));
tools.notes: Words not in the bag vocabulary are ignored. Transformer tokenizers have their own encode method (bertTokenizer).

tools.name: fitlda
tools.description: Fits a latent Dirichlet allocation topic model to a bag-of-words model or count matrix, discovering a given number of topics as word distributions and each document's topic mixture.
tools.usage:
mdl = fitlda(bag, numTopics)
mdl = fitlda(counts, numTopics)
mdl = fitlda(___, Name=Value)
tools.notes: Returns an ldaModel with TopicWordProbabilities, DocumentTopicProbabilities and CorpusTopicProbabilities. Use logp for perplexity-based selection of numTopics, predict/transform for new documents and resume to continue fitting.

tools.name: fitlsa
tools.description: Fits a latent semantic analysis model: a truncated SVD of the (weighted) document-term matrix that projects documents into a low-dimensional semantic space. Useful for dimensionality reduction and document similarity.
tools.usage:
mdl = fitlsa(bag, numComponents)
mdl = fitlsa(counts, numComponents)
mdl = fitlsa(___, FeatureStrengthExponent=p)

parameters.name: FeatureStrengthExponent
parameters.description: Exponent applied to singular values when computing document scores (default 2).

tools.notes: Returns an lsaModel with DocumentScores, WordScores, ComponentWeights and Vocabulary. Unlike LDA, components can have negative weights.

tools.name: vaderSentimentScores
tools.description: Computes sentiment scores with the rule- and lexicon-based VADER algorithm, returning a compound score between -1 (most negative) and +1 (most positive) per document. It handles negations, intensifiers, capitalization and emoticons and suits short social-media text.
tools.usage:
compoundScores = vaderSentimentScores(documents)
[compoundScores, positiveScores, negativeScores, neutralScores] = vaderSentimentScores(documents, Name=Value)

parameters.name: SentimentLexicon
parameters.description: Table with Token and SentimentScore columns to replace the default VADER lexicon.

parameters.name: Boosters / Dampeners / Negations
parameters.description: Custom intensifier, dampener and negation word lists.

tools.example:
documents = tokenizedDocument(["The service was GREAT!!! :)"; "Not good, the pump failed again."]);
scores = vaderSentimentScores(documents)
tools.notes: English only. Do not remove stop words or punctuation beforehand, because negations and exclamation marks carry sentiment.

tools.name: ratioSentimentScores
tools.description: Computes sentiment scores as the ratio of positive to negative word counts using a user-supplied sentiment lexicon. Use it for domain-specific sentiment where you define which words are positive or negative.
tools.usage: [compoundScores, positiveScores, negativeScores] = ratioSentimentScores(documents, sentimentWords)

parameters.name: sentimentWords
parameters.description: Table with variables Token and SentimentScore (positive values for positive words, negative for negative words).

tools.notes: Build domain lexicons from seed words with word-embedding similarity. Documents without lexicon words get NaN scores.

tools.name: bert
tools.description: Loads a pretrained BERT transformer as a dlnetwork together with its matching bertTokenizer. Use it for feature extraction, fine-tuning or as the backbone of a bertDocumentClassifier.
tools.usage:
[net, tokenizer] = bert
[net, tokenizer] = bert(Model=modelName)
tools.example:
[net, tokenizer] = bert(Model="tiny");
[tokenCodes, segments] = encode(tokenizer, "MATLAB is great for text analytics.");
tools.notes: Introduced R2023b. Requires the corresponding Text Analytics Toolbox Model for BERT support package (downloaded via Add-On Explorer on first use). Also requires Deep Learning Toolbox.

tools.name: bertTokenizer
tools.description: WordPiece tokenizer used by BERT models. It converts text into token codes and segment indices (encode), splits text into subwords, and maps codes back to tokens (decode).
tools.usage:
tokenizer = bertTokenizer(vocabulary)
[tokenCodes, segments] = encode(tokenizer, str)
words = decode(tokenizer, tokenCodes)

parameters.name: vocabulary
parameters.description: String array of WordPiece vocabulary (or obtain the tokenizer from bert).

tools.notes: Introduced R2023b. bpeTokenizer provides byte-pair encoding for GPT-style models. Encoded sequences include [CLS] and [SEP] tokens.

tools.name: trainBERTDocumentClassifier
tools.description: Fine-tunes a BERT document classifier (bertDocumentClassifier) on labeled text. It handles tokenization and batching internally, so you only provide documents, labels and Deep Learning Toolbox training options.
tools.usage:
mdlTrained = trainBERTDocumentClassifier(documents, targets, mdl, options)
mdlTrained = trainBERTDocumentClassifier(tbl, mdl, options)

parameters.name: documents
parameters.description: String array, cellstr or tokenizedDocument array of training text.

tools.notes: Introduced R2023b. A GPU is strongly recommended. Choose a smaller Model ("tiny", "mini") in bertDocumentClassifier for faster training.

tools.name: fastTextWordEmbedding
tools.description: Loads a pretrained 300-dimensional fastText English word embedding (about one million words trained on 16 billion tokens). Embeddings map words to dense vectors whose geometry reflects meaning.
tools.usage: emb = fastTextWordEmbedding
tools.notes: Requires the Text Analytics Toolbox Model for fastText English 16 Billion Token Word Embedding support package. Use trainWordEmbedding for domain-specific corpora.

tools.name: trainWordEmbedding
tools.description: Trains a word embedding (word2vec-style skip-gram or CBOW with subword n-grams) on a text file or tokenized documents. Use it when pretrained embeddings do not cover your domain vocabulary.
tools.usage:
emb = trainWordEmbedding(filename)
emb = trainWordEmbedding(documents)
emb = trainWordEmbedding(___, Name=Value)

parameters.name: NumEpochs / MinCount
parameters.description: Training passes and minimum word frequency.

tools.notes: Save and reload embeddings with writeWordEmbedding/readWordEmbedding (word2vec text format).

tools.name: word2vec
tools.description: Maps words to their embedding vectors using a wordEmbedding model. Out-of-vocabulary words return NaN rows. Combine with vec2word for nearest-word lookups and analogy arithmetic.
tools.usage:
M = word2vec(emb, words)
words = vec2word(emb, M)
words = vec2word(emb, M, k)

parameters.name: words
parameters.description: String array of words; M has one row per word.

parameters.name: k
parameters.description: Number of nearest words for vec2word.

tools.notes: Check isVocabularyWord(emb, words) before lookup. Average word vectors or use documentEmbedding to get document-level features.

tools.name: wordEncoding
tools.description: Creates a word encoding model that maps each vocabulary word to an integer index and back. It is used with doc2sequence and wordEmbeddingLayer to feed text into deep learning sequence networks.
tools.usage:
enc = wordEncoding(documents)
enc = wordEncoding(documents, Name=Value)
enc = wordEncoding(words)

parameters.name: MaxNumWords
parameters.description: Keep only the most frequent words.

tools.example:
enc = wordEncoding(trainDocs, MaxNumWords=5000);
idx = word2ind(enc, "pump")
ind2word(enc, 1)
enc.NumWords
tools.notes: Build the encoding on training data only. Unknown words are handled by doc2sequence (UnknownWord) or the layer's OOVMode.

tools.name: doc2sequence
tools.description: Converts tokenized documents into numeric sequences for deep learning: word indices when given a wordEncoding, or embedding-vector sequences when given a wordEmbedding. Sequences can be padded or truncated to a fixed length.
tools.usage:
sequences = doc2sequence(enc, documents)
sequences = doc2sequence(emb, documents)
sequences = doc2sequence(___, Name=Value)
tools.notes: Output is a cell array: 1-by-L index rows for encodings, D-by-L matrices for embeddings. Left padding is best for LSTMs with OutputMode="last".

tools.name: wordEmbeddingLayer
tools.description: Deep learning layer that maps word indices to learnable dense vectors. It is the first layer after sequenceInputLayer in LSTM/GRU/CNN text classifiers and can be initialized from pretrained embedding weights.
tools.usage:
layer = wordEmbeddingLayer(dimension, numWords)
layer = wordEmbeddingLayer(___, Name=Value)

parameters.name: Weights
parameters.description: Initial dimension-by-(numWords+1) weight matrix, e.g. from word2vec of a pretrained embedding.

tools.notes: Set WeightLearnRateFactor=0 to freeze pretrained vectors. Requires Deep Learning Toolbox.

tools.name: extractSummary
tools.description: Produces an extractive summary by scoring documents (typically sentences) with TextRank, LexRank or maximal marginal relevance and returning the most important ones.
tools.usage:
summary = extractSummary(documents)
[summary, scores] = extractSummary(documents, Name=Value)

parameters.name: SummarySize
parameters.description: Fraction in (0,1) of documents (default 0.1), an integer count, or Inf.

tools.notes: Introduced R2020a. Split text into sentences first; the function selects existing documents, it does not generate new text. textrankScores, lexrankScores and mmrScores expose the raw scores.

tools.name: rakeKeywords
tools.description: Extracts keywords and key phrases with the RAKE (Rapid Automatic Keyword Extraction) algorithm, which splits text at stop words and punctuation and scores candidate phrases by word co-occurrence.
tools.usage:
tbl = rakeKeywords(documents)
tbl = rakeKeywords(documents, Name=Value)

parameters.name: Delimiters / MergingDelimiters
parameters.description: Tokens that split candidates (punctuation) and that can join adjacent keywords (stop words).

parameters.name: IgnoreKeywordCase
parameters.description: Merge keywords differing only in case.

tools.notes: Output table columns: Keyword (string array of tokens), DocumentNumber, Score. Do not remove stop words beforehand, since RAKE uses them as delimiters.

tools.name: textrankKeywords
tools.description: Extracts keywords using TextRank: a graph of co-occurring candidate words (by default nouns and adjectives) is ranked with PageRank, and adjacent top words are merged into key phrases.
tools.usage:
tbl = textrankKeywords(documents)
tbl = textrankKeywords(documents, Name=Value)

parameters.name: PartOfSpeech
parameters.description: Parts of speech allowed as candidates.

tools.notes: Part-of-speech details are added automatically if missing. Compare with rakeKeywords, which does not need POS tags.

tools.name: bm25Similarity
tools.description: Computes document-to-document or document-to-query relevance scores with the Okapi BM25 ranking function (and variants BM11, BM15, BM25+). It is the classic scoring method for keyword search and retrieval-augmented pipelines.
tools.usage:
similarities = bm25Similarity(documents)
similarities = bm25Similarity(documents, queries)
similarities = bm25Similarity(bag, queries)
similarities = bm25Similarity(___, Name=Value)

parameters.name: IDFCorrection / DocumentLengthCorrection
parameters.description: Corrections used by the BM25+ variant.

tools.notes: Output is numDocuments-by-numQueries. Preprocess queries the same way as documents (lowercase, stop words, stemming).

tools.name: cosineSimilarity
tools.description: Computes cosine similarity between documents (via bag-of-words counts), between documents and queries, or between rows of arbitrary feature matrices such as tf-idf, LSA scores or embeddings.
tools.usage:
similarities = cosineSimilarity(documents)
similarities = cosineSimilarity(documents, queries)
similarities = cosineSimilarity(bag)
similarities = cosineSimilarity(M)
similarities = cosineSimilarity(M1, M2)

parameters.name: M, M1, M2
parameters.description: Numeric feature matrices with one row per document.

tools.notes: Values range from 0 to 1 for non-negative features. For sentence embeddings use documentEmbedding + embed, then cosineSimilarity on the vectors.

tools.name: textscatter
tools.description: Creates a 2-D scatter plot of text labels, automatically hiding overlapping labels based on density. It is commonly used to visualize word embeddings reduced with tsne or document clusters.
tools.usage:
textscatter(x, y, str)
textscatter(XY, str)
textscatter(___, Name=Value)
ts = textscatter(___)

parameters.name: ColorData
parameters.description: Colors or categorical groups for the labels.

parameters.name: TextDensityPercentage
parameters.description: Percentage of labels to show in dense areas (default 60).

tools.notes: textscatter3 is the 3-D version. wordcloud (base MATLAB) visualizes word frequencies instead of positions.

tools.name: splitTextChunks
tools.description: Splits documents recursively into text chunks of a target length, preferring paragraph, then sentence, then token boundaries. It prepares long documents for embedding and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) workflows.
tools.usage:
chunkTable = splitTextChunks(str)
chunkTable = splitTextChunks(t)
chunkTable = splitTextChunks(___, Name=Value)

parameters.name: str / t
parameters.description: Text, or a table whose first text variable holds documents (other variables are carried along as metadata).

parameters.name: TargetLength
parameters.description: Target number of characters per chunk (default 4000).

parameters.name: SplitLevels
parameters.description: Hierarchy of split levels, default ["paragraph","sentence","token"]; "character" also allowed.

tools.notes: Recent addition (R2026a). Related chunking functions: splitMarkdownSections, splitHTMLSections, addTextChunkOverlap, joinSimilarTextChunks, formatTextChunks.
